newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Harel top small cap among Israeli funds.
newsitem.headline: Harel top small cap among Israeli funds.

text.p: Harel Hamishmar Investments 5, an insurer, was the small capitalisation stock most widely held by Israeli mutual funds at the end of 1996, Meitav Investments and Securities said on Wednesday.

It said the nine biggest mutual funds, whose combined assets represent 90 percent of all Israeli mutual fund assets, held 49 million shekels of Harel. In second place was Azorim Properties in which the funds held 33 million shekels of equity.
Meitav, a broker and fund manager that tracks the mutual funds industry, defined small cap as stocks traded in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange's karam system.
The other stocks among the top five held by the funds were Bayside 1, Ackerstein Zvi 5 and Bayside 5.
Meitav noted that of the 870 karam stocks listed in the exchange, 166 were not held by mutual funds at all.
Among heavy capitalisation stocks, Meitav reported earlier this week that Koor Industries Ltd was the most widely held by the funds.
